Sample.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/6] Of the Time 1 participants, 57 % (n = 446) also completed the survey at Time 2. Longitudinal respondents differed significantly (p.05) from the baseline-only respondents (n = 339) on only two of the study variables described below: Longitudinal respondents were significantly more likely to be female than non-longitudinal respondents (76 vs. 70 %), and reported significantly higher levels of PA at baseline (3.76 vs. 3.65, respectively).
